server_entry.name: Rain Bird
server_entry.desc: Local-network control of Rain Bird sprinkler controllers (ESP-Me and other LNK WiFi models) using the pyrainbird library: zone on/off with run time, stop all, rain delay, rain sensor, water budget (read-only) and program start.

readme_body:
# Rain Bird for eisy / IoX

Local-network control of Rain Bird sprinkler controllers through the Rain Bird WiFi module (**LNK**). Built on the open-source [`pyrainbird`](https://github.com/allenporter/pyrainbird) library (MIT). It talks directly to the controller's IP address - no Rain Bird cloud account is involved. Developed for an **ESP-Me**; other controllers that use the same protocol (ESP-TM2, ESP-ME3, ...) may work too, but only an ESP-TM2 is listed as fully verified by the library authors.

> **LNK2 modules:** the released `pyrainbird` 6.0.2 only speaks plain HTTP (LNK). LNK2 modules need HTTPS, which only newer, unreleased library code supports. When a newer release is published the plugin will use it automatically (`create_controller`).

## Settings

Only two: **host** (the WiFi module's IP address) and **password**. There is no user name or email.

## What you get

**Rain Bird Plugin** (controller node): connection status and a *Discover* command.

**Rain Bird <model>** (one node):
| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Watering | Idle / Watering (any zone running) |
| Rain Delay | days remaining |
| Rain Sensor | Clear / Rain Detected |
| Water Budget | seasonal adjust, % (read-only) |

Commands: *Stop All Watering*, *Set Rain Delay* (0-14 days), *Run Program* (A-D).

**One node per zone**, named with the names you enter in the configuration:
| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Zone State | Off / Running |
| Run Time | minutes used when the zone is turned on (1-240) |

Commands: *On / Run Zone* (optional minutes, defaults to the node's Run Time), *Off / Stop Watering*, *Set Run Time*.

## Setup

1. Install the plugin and open its configuration page.
2. Enter **host** (reserve the address in your router) and **password** (the one from the Rain Bird app).
3. Optionally add rows under **Zone names**.
4. Restart the plugin if nodes do not appear; then press *Discover*.

## Good to know

* The controller handles **one client at a time**. Opening the Rain Bird app while the plugin is polling can cause a brief "busy" message; the plugin retries up to 3 times.
* Zone status polls every 30 s; rain delay, rain sensor and water budget every 5 min.
* The Rain Bird protocol can only *stop all* watering, so a zone's *Off* command stops watering only if that zone is currently running.
* **Safety pauses** (shown as a notice on the plugin page): a rejected password pauses polling until you save the configuration; 3 undecodable replies in a row (usually a wrong password) pause for 16 minutes; 3 network failures in a row pause for 2 minutes.
* On every start the plugin removes any banner it did not create itself and names its controller node "Rain Bird Plugin", so leftovers from another plugin that previously used the same slot disappear.
* Water budget is read from program A. Changing it is not supported by the released library - use the Rain Bird app.
* Program letters A-D are sent as program numbers 0-3 (not verified against hardware - check on first use).
* Schedules/programs themselves are not edited by this plugin.

## Requirements

`pyrainbird>=6.0.2` (installed automatically).

override_bodies.start:
def start(self):
        import rainbird_nodes as rb
        rb.LOGGER.info('Rain Bird plugin starting')
        rb.cleanup_foreign(self.poly, self)
        rb._S['started'] = True
        rb.bootstrap(self.poly, self.address)
override_bodies.stop:
def stop(self):
        import rainbird_nodes as rb
        rb.LOGGER.info('Rain Bird plugin stopping')
        rb._S['started'] = False
        rb.shutdown()

def customTypedDataHandler(self, custom_params):
        import rainbird_nodes as rb
        self.CustomTypedData.load(custom_params)
        rb.set_zone_names(self.poly, custom_params)

tests.test_rainbird_nodes.py:
import os
import sys
import time

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))

import rainbird_nodes as rb  # noqa: E402


class FakePoly:
    def getValidName(self, name):
        return name


def _reset():
    rb._S.update(blocked_until=0.0, pending_notice=None, fail_pw=0, fail_net=0,
                 ctrl=None, reset=False, host='', password='', zones=[], names={})


def test_zone_address():
    assert rb.zone_address(3) == 'zone3'
    assert len(rb.zone_address(40)) <= 14


def test_cmd_int_value():
    assert rb._cmd_int({'value': '12'}) == 12
    assert rb._cmd_int({'value': 7.0}) == 7


def test_cmd_int_query_fallback():
    assert rb._cmd_int({'query': {'': '5'}}) == 5
    assert rb._cmd_int({'query': {'duration': '9'}}) == 9


def test_cmd_int_missing_or_bad():
    assert rb._cmd_int(None) is None
    assert rb._cmd_int({}) is None
    assert rb._cmd_int({'value': 'abc'}) is None


def test_clamp():
    assert rb._clamp(500, 10, 200) == 200
    assert rb._clamp(-1, 0, 14) == 0
    assert rb._clamp(30, 1, 240) == 30


def test_zone_names_and_defaults():
    _reset()
    rb.set_zone_names(FakePoly(), {'zone_names': [
        {'zone': 1.0, 'name': '  Front Lawn '},
        {'zone': 2, 'name': ''},
    ]})
    assert rb.zone_name(1) == 'Front Lawn'
    assert rb.zone_name(2) == 'Zone 2'
    assert rb.zone_name(3) == 'Zone 3'


def test_zone_names_bad_input_is_ignored():
    _reset()
    rb.set_zone_names(FakePoly(), None)
    assert rb.zone_name(1) == 'Zone 1'
    rb.set_zone_names(FakePoly(), {'zone_names': [{'zone': 'x', 'name': 'Oops'}]})
    assert rb.zone_name(1) == 'Zone 1'


def test_classify():
    class RainbirdApiException(Exception):
        pass

    class RainbirdAuthException(RainbirdApiException):
        pass

    class RainbirdCodingException(Exception):
        pass

    class RainbirdDeviceBusyException(RainbirdApiException):
        pass

    assert rb._classify(RainbirdAuthException()) == 'auth'
    assert rb._classify(RainbirdCodingException()) == 'password'
    assert rb._classify(RainbirdDeviceBusyException()) == 'busy'
    assert rb._classify(RainbirdApiException()) == 'network'
    assert rb._classify(TimeoutError()) == 'network'
    assert rb._classify(AttributeError('x')) == 'bug'


def test_three_password_failures_pause_for_sixteen_minutes():
    _reset()
    rb._record_failure('password')
    rb._record_failure('password')
    assert not rb._blocked()
    rb._record_failure('password')
    assert rb._blocked()
    assert 15 * 60 < rb._S['blocked_until'] - time.time() <= 16 * 60
    assert rb._S['pending_notice']
    # after the pause a single further failure pauses again
    assert rb._S['fail_pw'] == rb.FAILURES_BEFORE_PAUSE - 1


def test_explicit_auth_rejection_pauses_until_settings_saved():
    _reset()
    rb._record_failure('auth')
    assert rb._blocked()
    assert rb._S['blocked_until'] == float('inf')
    rb.configure(FakePoly_with_notices(), 'h', 'p')
    assert not rb._blocked()


def test_three_network_failures_pause_for_two_minutes():
    _reset()
    for _ in range(3):
        rb._record_failure('network')
    assert rb._blocked()
    assert 100 < rb._S['blocked_until'] - time.time() <= 120


def test_busy_and_bug_do_not_count():
    _reset()
    for _ in range(5):
        rb._record_failure('busy')
        rb._record_failure('bug')
    assert not rb._blocked()
    assert rb._S['fail_pw'] == 0 and rb._S['fail_net'] == 0


class FakeNotices(dict):
    def delete(self, key):
        self.pop(key, None)


class FakePoly_with_notices(FakePoly):
    def __init__(self):
        self.Notices = FakeNotices()


class FakeController:
    address = 'ctl'

    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        self.renamed_to = None

    def rename(self, new_name):
        self.renamed_to = new_name


def test_cleanup_foreign_removes_only_other_plugins_notices_and_renames():
    poly = FakePoly_with_notices()
    poly.Notices['midea_conn'] = 'old NetHome Plus banner'
    poly.Notices['config'] = 'mine'
    poly.Notices['rainbird'] = 'mine too'
    ctl = FakeController('NetHome Plus Controller')
    rb.cleanup_foreign(poly, ctl)
    assert set(poly.Notices) == {'config', 'rainbird'}
    assert ctl.renamed_to == 'Rain Bird Plugin'
    assert ctl.name == 'Rain Bird Plugin'


def test_cleanup_foreign_leaves_correct_name_alone():
    poly = FakePoly_with_notices()
    ctl = FakeController('Rain Bird Plugin')
    rb.cleanup_foreign(poly, ctl)
    assert ctl.renamed_to is None


def test_call_retries_busy_then_succeeds(monkeypatch):
    _reset()

    class RainbirdDeviceBusyException(Exception):
        pass

    class Fake:
        calls = 0

        async def get_rain_delay(self):
            Fake.calls += 1
            if Fake.calls < 3:
                raise RainbirdDeviceBusyException()
            return 4

    rb._S.update(host='h', password='p', ctrl=Fake())
    monkeypatch.setattr(rb.time, 'sleep', lambda seconds: None)
    assert rb.call('get_rain_delay') == 4
    assert Fake.calls == 3


def test_call_refuses_when_not_configured():
    _reset()
    try:
        rb.call('get_rain_delay')
        assert False, 'expected RuntimeError'
    except RuntimeError:
        pass

custom_param_docs:
Rain Bird plugin configuration

This plugin talks directly to your Rain Bird WiFi module (LNK) over your home network. No Rain Bird cloud account is used. There are only two settings: host and password. There is no user name or email.

host

The IP address of the Rain Bird WiFi module, for example 192.168.1.50.

  • Find it in your router's list of connected devices (look for a device named like Rain Bird or LNK).
  • Strongly recommended: give the module a DHCP reservation (fixed address) in your router so the address never changes.
  • Enter just the address - no http:// and no trailing slash.

password

The password you set for the controller in the Rain Bird app when you added it. It is the same password the app uses to talk to the controller locally.

Careful: some Rain Bird modules lock out local access for 15 minutes after 3 wrong passwords. To avoid that, this plugin stops polling after repeated password-type failures and shows a notice instead of retrying. Fix the password and save to try again.

Zone names

Use the Zone names list (below the fields above) to give each zone a friendly name, for example zone 1 = Front Lawn. Zones you do not list are called "Zone 1", "Zone 2", and so on. Renaming takes effect on the existing nodes right away.

Good to know

  • The controller can only talk to one app at a time. If you open the Rain Bird app while watering is being controlled here you may see a brief "busy" message in the plugin log; the plugin retries automatically.
  • Zone status is checked every 30 seconds; rain delay, rain sensor and water budget every 5 minutes.
  • Water budget is shown for information only; change it in the Rain Bird app.
  • If the controller drops off the network now and then, try putting the WiFi module on a dedicated 2.4 GHz-only network.
